security_hardening.title: Enable Electron Sandbox Mode for Defense-in-Depth
security_hardening.description: The Electron main window is configured with sandbox: false in apps/frontend/src/main/index.ts (line 66). While contextIsolation is enabled and nodeIntegration is disabled, the sandbox provides an additional security layer by restricting the renderer process at the OS level.
security_hardening.rationale: The Electron sandbox limits what code running in the renderer process can do at the operating system level. Without it, a compromised renderer (e.g., via XSS in loaded content) has more system access. This is important since the app loads external fonts from fonts.googleapis.com and may render external release notes.
security_hardening.currentRisk: Renderer process has fewer OS-level restrictions than recommended. If an attacker could execute code in the renderer context, they would have more capabilities than necessary.
security_hardening.remediation: Enable sandbox mode by setting sandbox: true in webPreferences. Review any preload script functionality that requires sandbox: false and refactor to use IPC handlers in the main process instead. Test PTY terminal integration thoroughly as node-pty may need adjustments.

security_hardening.title: Add Fallback Security Warning for Unencrypted Token Storage
security_hardening.description: In apps/frontend/src/main/claude-profile/token-encryption.ts, when Electron's safeStorage encryption is unavailable, OAuth tokens are stored in plaintext with only a console.warn. Users have no visibility that their credentials are stored insecurely.
security_hardening.rationale: OAuth tokens provide access to Claude AI services and potentially sensitive user data. Silent fallback to plaintext storage without user notification is a security anti-pattern. Users should be able to make informed decisions about their credential security.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
security_hardening.currentRisk: On systems where safeStorage is unavailable (e.g., certain Linux configurations without a keyring), OAuth tokens are stored in plaintext in settings.json, readable by any process with file access.
security_hardening.remediation: 1) Emit an IPC event to show a prominent UI warning when encryption fails. 2) Consider a fallback encryption using a machine-derived key (hardware ID + salt). 3) Add isTokenStoredSecurely() API for the UI to show security status. 4) Log security audit events when fallback occurs.

security_hardening.title: Add npm Dependency Vulnerability Scanning to CI Pipeline
security_hardening.description: The .github/workflows/quality-security.yml workflow runs CodeQL and Bandit for code analysis, but lacks npm audit or any JavaScript/TypeScript dependency vulnerability scanning. The frontend has 35+ runtime dependencies that could contain known CVEs.
security_hardening.rationale: Third-party npm packages are a common attack vector. Packages like electron, react-markdown, @xterm/xterm, and various @radix-ui components should be monitored for vulnerabilities. Supply chain attacks on npm are well-documented.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components
security_hardening.currentRisk: Vulnerable npm dependencies may exist without automated detection. The project uses Electron v39, xterm v6, and many UI libraries that should be continuously monitored.
security_hardening.remediation:
Add an npm audit job to quality-security.yml:

```yaml
npm-security:
  name: NPM Dependency Audit
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '24'
    - run: cd apps/frontend && npm ci
    - run: cd apps/frontend && npm audit --audit-level=high
```

For Python, add pip-audit to scan apps/backend/requirements.txt.

security_hardening.title: Replace Custom HTML Sanitization with DOMPurify
security_hardening.description: Two React components use dangerouslySetInnerHTML with custom regex-based HTML escaping: AppUpdateNotification.tsx (release notes) and AdvancedSettings.tsx. While the current escaping handles basic XSS (<, >, &), regex-based sanitization can miss edge cases.
security_hardening.rationale: Release notes come from external sources (GitHub releases API). Custom sanitizers often miss edge cases like malformed UTF-8 sequences, HTML5 entities, or SVG-based XSS. DOMPurify has been extensively tested against thousands of XSS vectors.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
security_hardening.currentRisk: If a crafted release note bypasses the regex sanitization, XSS could occur in the Electron renderer context. The current sanitization escapes &, <, > before processing, which is good, but a whitelist approach is safer.

security_hardening.title: Add Python Dependency Hash Pinning for Supply Chain Security
security_hardening.description: The apps/backend/requirements.txt and tests/requirements-test.txt specify dependencies with version ranges but lack cryptographic hash pinning. This leaves the project vulnerable to supply chain attacks where a malicious version could replace a legitimate one.
security_hardening.rationale: Supply chain attacks on Python packages (e.g., typosquatting, account compromise) are increasing. Hash pinning ensures that only verified, known-good versions are installed. Critical packages like claude-agent-sdk, graphiti-core handle AI credentials.
security_hardening.vulnerability: CWE-494: Download of Code Without Integrity Check
security_hardening.currentRisk: Dependencies are installed without cryptographic verification. A compromised PyPI package could inject malicious code into the build or development environment.
security_hardening.remediation:
Use pip-compile from pip-tools to generate requirements with hashes:
```bash
pip install pip-tools
pip-compile --generate-hashes requirements.in -o requirements.txt
pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt
```

Alternatively, adopt Poetry or PDM with lockfiles. Add pip-audit to CI for ongoing vulnerability scanning:
```yaml
- run: pip install pip-audit && pip-audit -r apps/backend/requirements.txt
```

securityPositives: Electron configured with contextIsolation: true and nodeIntegration: false
Content Security Policy defined in index.html with reasonable defaults
OAuth tokens use Electron safeStorage API when available
GitHub Actions workflow includes CodeQL and Bandit security scanning
Comprehensive secret scanning patterns in apps/backend/security/scan_secrets.py
Authentication intentionally excludes API keys to prevent silent billing
subprocess.spawn() uses array arguments (not shell=True) throughout codebase
Filtered environment variables in subprocess-runner.ts prevent secret leakage
analysisNotes: CSP IS configured in index.html (previous analysis was incorrect)
CSP includes 'unsafe-inline' for styles which is acceptable for this use case
The sandbox: false setting is required for node-pty terminal integration
No high-severity CVEs detected in current dependency versions
GitHub API calls go through gh CLI, inheriting its authentication model
